content:
amanda: FYI customer hitting 401 for SSE streaming only. Non-streaming completions with same token are fine. Request ID: r-abc123. Region: us-west2. They say browser fetch with Cookie works but curl fails. Any quick repro steps?

sam: Can you get the exact curl they ran? often it's a header/cookie mismatch for streaming. Also please include the token or cookie redacted and the raw response body.

amanda: Customer pasted this (redacted):
```
curl -N -H 'Cookie: session=eyJhbGci...' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
They get HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized and no SSE lines.

sam: Two things to try: 1) Use Authorization header instead of Cookie when calling our hosted API (cookies are only forwarded in certain proxy configs). 2) Add SSE/streaming headers and no-buffer flags. Example repro template:
```
curl -v --http2 --no-buffer -N \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live_XXXXXXX' \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -H 'Cache-Control: no-cache' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: r-abc123' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4t", "input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat
```
Use `--trace-ascii trace.txt` if you need a network-level trace.

ingrid: quick note from runtime side — cookies set by the customer domain (example.com) won't be forwarded to api.redwood.ai unless the cookie was created for that domain and Secure/SameSite flags allow it. If browser fetch works it might be the browser attaching a cookie we don't see on direct curl. That explains the 401.

sam: Also watch for token expiry — server logs show cases like: `2026-02-10T12:34:56.789Z auth error: token_expired req=r-abc123` — if you can paste a snippet of our server's x-request-id and the time we can correlate.

customer-jess: Tried your Authorization header example (redacted token). With the exact curl above I now see: `HTTP/2 200\ncontent-type: text/event-stream` and SSE payloads: `data: {"id":"m-1","text":"Hello"}\n\n`
Works for me now.

amanda: Great — can you also attach the curl -v logs or the `trace.txt` just in case it reappears? If you prefer, you can upload to the debug-bucket and share the link.

customer-jess: Uploaded trace to https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-debug/customer-uploads/r-abc123/trace.txt — trace shows TLS handshake + 200 when using Authorization header, 401 when cookie.

ingsrid: (small correction) — please note we redact tokens in logs; if you want us to rotate the key for you, we can issue a short-lived key to test.

sam: Closing checklist: - Verified repro with `--http2 --no-buffer -N` + Authorization header - customer uploaded trace and we correlated request id r-abc123 in logs - root cause: cookie not forwarded in direct curl -> 401. Recommendation: use Authorization header or generate ephemeral key for non-browser clients.

support-bot: Thanks! If this resolves your issue, react with :white_check_mark: and we'll close the ticket. For full debug bundle instructions see https://docs.redwood.ai/support/debug-bundles

amanda: Customer confirmed in thread they are good to close. Marking resolved. :thumbsup:
